attempts.label: DANDI:000943
attempts.paper_title: Task-anchored grid cell firing is selectively associated with successful path integration-dependent behaviour
attempts.entry_title: Task-anchored grid cell firing and path integration (Clark and Nolan 2024)
attempts.description: Surveys dandiset 000943, which holds the raw tetrode signal and position series of the open arena and virtual track sessions of Clark and Nolan (2024), checks its description against the values, and measures what testing the paper's claims would take. The dandiset holds no sorted units, which every claim needs, and sorting its 976 GB of raw signal does not fit the limits, so every claim is blocked.

notebooks.title: Clark and Nolan (2024) on dandiset 000943, data check and size of the spike sorting

outcomes.statement: Of 1881 MEC neurons recorded in nine mice, 103 were classified as grid cells from their open arena firing, 11.4 +- 17.4 grid cells per mouse, 0.4 to 9.5% of each mouse's neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 1; Supplementary file 1
outcomes.quote: we identified 103/1881 neurons as grid cells (11.4±17.4 grid cells/mouse, range 0.4–9.5%, Supplementary file 1 )
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds no sorted units (no file has a units table or any processed data), and the claim needs single units. Making them as the paper did means streaming the raw signal of every recording day, sorting the open arena and VR recordings of a day together with MountainSort and curating the clusters by isolation, noise overlap and peak SNR (Methods, Spike sorting). Streaming alone, at the rate measured in the executed notebook (76.4 MB/s with 16 processes; it varies by several percent between runs), takes 2.3 h for the 638 GB of the recording days (478 files) of the 239 usable 200 cm VR sessions of the nine mice that have an open arena session the same day, which are a superset of the paper's 215 sessions (2.1 h when the size is scaled to 215 sessions), and 3.6 h for all 976 GB, against the protocol's limit of 60 min for a notebook (docs/protocol.md, Author, step 3); this is a lower bound, as sorting time comes on top and was not measured. The sort was not started. Grid cells are then classified from each unit's open arena rate map with 1000 shuffles per unit, which also needs the units. Even with units, the open arena rate maps would rest on position columns whose meaning is inferred from their ranges (the nine columns are undescribed), and 18 of the 41 open arena sessions of M1, one of the paper's nine mice, span only 67.5 to 89.8 cm against the 100 x 100 cm arena the files describe, so a re-sort could still meet a metadata_insufficient block.

outcomes.statement: Per mouse, the numbers of cells, sessions, trials per session and grid cells are as in Supplementary file 1, in total 1881 cells and 215 sessions, with most grid cells from M11 (53) and M14 (26).
outcomes.source: Supplementary file 1

outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds no sorted units (no file has a units table or any processed data), and the claim needs single units. Making them as the paper did means streaming the raw signal of every recording day, sorting the open arena and VR recordings of a day together with MountainSort and curating the clusters by isolation, noise overlap and peak SNR (Methods, Spike sorting). Streaming alone, at the rate measured in the executed notebook (76.4 MB/s with 16 processes; it varies by several percent between runs), takes 2.3 h for the 638 GB of the recording days (478 files) of the 239 usable 200 cm VR sessions of the nine mice that have an open arena session the same day, which are a superset of the paper's 215 sessions (2.1 h when the size is scaled to 215 sessions), and 3.6 h for all 976 GB, against the protocol's limit of 60 min for a notebook (docs/protocol.md, Author, step 3); this is a lower bound, as sorting time comes on top and was not measured. The sort was not started. It also depends on grid-cell-count. The parts that need no units were compared in the data check, not as a test of the claim. The dandiset has 242 VR sessions on the 200 cm track with at least 10 trials for the nine mice (paper 215), 27 more, outside the claim's tolerance of 21.5; per mouse M1 11 (11), M3 30 (26), M6 21 (21), M7 28 (23), M10 25 (16), M11 35 (35), M12 28 (21), M13 27 (25), M14 37 (37), so five of nine are within 10% of the table and M3, M7, M10 and M12 exceed it by 15%, 22%, 56% and 33%. The mean over the nine mice of each mouse's mean trials per session is 183.9 (paper 179.1). The paper counts only sessions with kept units, which the dandiset cannot show, so the excess sessions may be sessions without kept units. Cells and grid cells per mouse need the units.

findings.statement: None of the 734 files holds sorted units, a units table, a trials table, reward times or any processed data; each holds only the raw 16-channel tetrode signal (30 kHz) and a position series. Every claim of the paper rests on units sorted with MountainSort, so none can be tested without sorting about 976 GB of raw signal. The paper's data are deposited at Edinburgh DataShare (the paper's data availability statement); this attempt did not use or inspect them. The dandiset's variableMeasured lists only ElectrodeGroup and ElectricalSeries, which is accurate.

The position series has the same description in every file, "position: cm, speed: cm/s, angle: degrees, trials: non-zero indexed, trial types: 0-beaconed, 1-nonbeaconed, 2-probe". The VR files hold three columns (position, trial number, trial type) and no speed or angle; the open arena files hold nine columns and no trials.

The nine columns of the open arena position series are not named. From their ranges, columns 1 and 3 appear to be x and y in cm, 2 and 4 the same in camera pixels, 5 head direction in degrees, 7 speed in cm/s, 0 and 8 times in s; column 6 (session minima from 33.4, maxima up to 37,697) could not be identified.

The files describe a 100 x 100 cm open arena, and in most sessions the x and y columns span 88.0 to 103.7 cm, but in 38 open arena sessions, 18 of M1's 41 and 20 of M2's 21, they span only 67.5 to 89.8 cm, so either the arena was smaller in these sessions or the position scaling differs; the files do not say which.

Two VR files have position for only part of the raw recording, sub-M13 ses-M13-D27-2021-06-15-11-43-42 (687 s of 2168 s, 21 trials) and sub-M15 ses-M15-D5-2021-05-14-12-46-13 (881 s of 1779 s, 14 trials). In the other 353 VR files the position series ends within 0.1 s of the raw signal.

In open arena files the position series usually runs past the end of the raw signal, by a median 2.9 s (5th to 95th percentile 1.2 to 9.5 s), and in 20 of 379 files the two differ by more than 10 s (up to 451.9 s longer and 178.2 s shorter). The files do not say how the position was aligned to the raw signal (the data collection text describes LED pulses, which are not in the files).

The dandiset holds 12 mice, 379 open arena and 355 VR files, 29 of them on tracks longer than 200 cm; the paper uses nine mice and the 200 cm track. For the nine mice it has 242 usable 200 cm VR sessions (at least 10 trials) against the 215 of the paper's summary table, with more sessions than the table by more than 10% for M3 (30 against 26), M7 (28, 23), M10 (25, 16) and M12 (28, 21), and slightly more for M13 (27, 25). Nothing in the dandiset marks which sessions the paper used. 48 recording days have only an open arena file and 24 only a VR file.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier also queried the archive API for every asset's metadata. It gave blocked, too_large for all 31 claims, agreeing with the record, and said data_missing could be argued but too_large is defensible since the raw data are present. It found no misreading of the paper in the claims file that affects these blocks. Other changes in reply: the helper docstring now says 100 ms bins for the multi-unit check (it said 1 s); shifted_contrast no longer wraps labels around the window ends and uses the same sign convention as lagged_corr (on synthetic data where activity leads speed by 5 bins both now give +5; in the M3 and M12 VR sessions the best shift is now +2.0 s, next to the +1.8 s and +1.7 s correlation peaks, and the other counts of the clock check are unchanged); a new data-check cell prints general/notes, experiment_description and protocol of one VR and one open arena file, which show the 200 cm track statement, the 4.7 cm/s stop speed over 100 ms and the 100 x 100 cm open field; the summary cell count was already 31.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier agreed with blocked, too_large for all 31 claims, found no misreading of the paper in the claims file that affects these blocks, and listed sentences the printed outputs do not support. Other changes in reply: cell 8 now prints the position range of the 326 sessions on the 200 cm track (0 to 200.0 cm), which cell 9 cites; cell 12 now prints each column's smallest session minimum (column 6 from 33.4) and the largest gaps between position and raw signal ends (451.9 s longer, 178.2 s shorter), and the findings give these; the 26.5 GB pickle (combined_cohorts.pkl), which no output or paper passage supports, is removed from the findings, README and summary, which now say only that the paper's data are at Edinburgh DataShare, from the paper's data availability statement; the quoted position description keeps its colons; the README says the 638 GB covers a superset of the paper's sessions and gives the scaled 2.1 h; in round 1, the reviewed field now says no misreading that affects these blocks, and the responses give the 72.4 MB/s then printed and the 67.5 to 89.8 cm extent. The round-1 reasons are kept in the verifier's words; the cells they cite (6, 8 and 19) are those of the round-1 notebook, now cells 8, 10 and 21. The verifier could not check the protocol's 60-minute limit beyond the quotation, as docs/protocol.md is not among its materials; nothing changed for that.

entries.name: 000943-clark-2024
entries.title: Task-anchored grid cell firing and path integration (Clark and Nolan 2024)
entries.description: Surveys dandiset 000943, which holds the raw tetrode signal and position series of the open arena and virtual track sessions of Clark and Nolan (2024), checks its description against the values, and measures what testing the paper's claims would take. The dandiset holds no sorted units, which every claim needs, and sorting its 976 GB of raw signal does not fit the limits, so every claim is blocked.
